Prokaryotic Chromosomes
Prokaryotic chromosome much simpler
Single, circular chromosome attached to inside of cell membrane 
Also compacted to fit within cell 
Region known as the nucleoid
Between cell divisions: DNA less compacted as chromatin
In preparation for/during cell division: DNA highlycompacted to form chromosomes
explanation: Prokaryotic chromosomes are structurally much simpler than eukaryotic ones. A prokaryote typically contains a single, circular chromosome that is attached to the inner surface of the cell membrane and compacted to fit within a region called the nucleoid. Between cell divisions, the DNA is less compacted and exists as chromatin. In preparation for and during cell division, the DNA condenses tightly into a highly compacted chromosome structure.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a prokaryotic chromosome?
opts: Multiple linear chromosomes enclosed in a nuclear membrane
A single, circular chromosome attached to the inside of the cell membrane
A double helix wrapped around histone proteins inside a nucleolus
A rod-shaped chromosome lacking a nucleoid region
questions.exp: Prokaryotic chromosomes are simpler, consisting of a single, circular chromosome attached to the inside of the cell membrane.
